mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5% simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered instances, or GDP growth rebounds above 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the unemployment rate falls below 5% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or industrial production rebounds by more than 2% in the subsequent month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) both rise simultaneously for three consecutive months, it indicates a high-inflation, high-rate environment that erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rise for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 2% within the next quarter.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 200,000 per month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or nonfarm payrolls decline by more than 100,000 in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on relationship exists between real retail sales (RSAFS) and S&P 500 forward returns: higher-than-expected monthly growth in real retail sales (RSAFS) predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate earnings optimism.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly above zero in periods where RSAFS growth exceeds its 12-month median, as measured by a one-tailed t-test (p > 0.10).
